speaker: Doctor
text: Does turning your head or rolling over in bed significantly worsen the spinning sensation, and do you experience any ringing in your ears or hearing loss? I would also like to examine your eyes for rapid, involuntary movements (nystagmus) when you look in different directions.

text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any hearing loss, ringing in your ears (tinnitus), or a feeling of fullness in one ear? I need to distinguish between benign positional vertigo and potential labyrinthitis or Meniere's disease. REQUEST TEST: Audiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recent viral illness and new bilateral hearing loss, this points toward vestibular neuritis or labyrinthitis rather than Meniere's. I need to visualize the inner ear and brainstem to rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_with_contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No acute abnormalities noted, specifically no signs of stroke or significant lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal and you have bilateral hearing loss following a viral illness, this presentation is most consistent with bilateral labyrinthitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Bilateral Labyrinthitis
